advice: Experiment: in both transpose/pack blocks `Llibxsmm_78` (the timed 512 path) and its matching packing sequence, replace the 32 separate `LD1W` plus pointer-add pairs with a counted row loop that loads one vector into a scratch row, advances the source by 2048 bytes, and repeats; then retain the existing grouped `MOV` transfers from z0–z31 to ZA. This changes packing control flow while preserving the same 32 input rows and ZA layout. Hypothesis: a compact load loop may reduce instruction-fetch and front-end pressure in this large repeated packing block. This is unverified advice; instruction count alone does not show a bottleneck or a speedup.
risks: The packing block may be bandwidth-bound, and looping can add branches or prevent overlap, so this may be slower. Preserve exact source bounds, 128 KiB scratch layout, pointer restoration, ZA row mapping, streaming-state balance, ABI, and BSD-3-Clause notice. Check assembler output and full correctness at n=512 plus general odd/tail sizes and n<=0 under the fixed FP32 tolerance. Then measure with fresh repeated paired controls under unchanged power settings; report spread and do not attribute noisy or joint outcomes to this proposal alone.
